newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica wants ACPC to end coffee export quotas.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica wants ACPC to end coffee export quotas.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meets next week in London, with Costa Rica firmly in favour of abandoning the cartel's export quota system which controls bean supplies, the top Costa Rican coffee official said Friday.

"We consider that the retention and quota scheme is not viable at this moment so we will be analyzing the situation to decide the steps to take in the immediate future," Ricardo Seevers, the new president opf the Costa Rican Coffee Institute told Reuters on Friday.
The ACPC meeting is scheduled for May 19-21 and will be immediately followed by a gathering of the International Coffee Organisation (ICO), ending May 23.

The ACPC has in place an export quota system for member nations, allocating volumes for sale per country per quarter. But given bullish prices pressure has been rising to end the quota scheme or to at least given more freedom in the quotas.
Seevers, who took over from Alonso Lara at the helm of the institute recently, said the spike in prices was as a result of the shortage of beans supplies.

Seevers said the ACPC meeting would center on dicussing the current situation and what could happen in the short and medium term. But he stressed Cost Rica was in favour of taking advantage of the high prices.
"High prices are a logical reaction of the market, but, not everything can go up indefinitely," Seevers added.
Seevers said that currently there were supply problems in Brazil, the world's top producer and Colombia, the number two, as well as in Indonesia and Central America.
Seevers estimated that stocks held by consumer nations currently were between 7.5 and 8 million 60-kg bags.
"Costa Rica remains loyal to the principle of ordering supply but inside a scheme of flexible and logical application," he added.
